findings.problem: The new field's comment says the config value is the default and that TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT overrides it at shutdown. findings.title: shutdown_drain_timeout config field is not read anywhere, so setting it has no effect

findings.fix_hint: add le=3600.0 to match the form clamp, as max_consecutive_failures does
findings.problem: The comment calls the form clamp (3600.0) the UI ceiling, but the model only has ge=1.0. A TOML-edited value such as 1e9 passes validation. It would hold shutdown well past the docker stop_grace_period of 90s, so SIGKILL would end the drain instead of the timeout (docker-compose.yml:24 and README.md:86 say the grace period must exceed the drain timeout). allow_inf_nan blocks inf but not very large finite values. The sibling field max_consecutive_failures sets both ge and le. pending: confirm whether a model-level le (for example le=3600.0) is intended to match the form clamp.
findings.title: No upper bound on the model; the 3600s ceiling is enforced only by the form clamp
findings.why_it_matters: A typo in a hand-edited config can push the drain past the container's kill deadline, so the graceful drain never finishes.

The field is not yet consumed anywhere (triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81 still reads TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT from the environment at import time, unchanged by this diff), so no new runtime attack surface is introduced. No injection, XSS, secrets, auth, data-exposure, path-traversal, SSRF, deserialization, or mass-assignment issues identified.

The diff adds one field to GeneralConfig (triggarr/models/config.py:139). It follows the existing bounded-Field pattern used in the same class, for example `max_consecutive_failures: int = Field(default=5, ge=1, le=100)` (SAFETY-03). It also matches the tag-comment convention (DEBT-06 next to SAFETY-03 and v2.2). Pattern consistency holds.

For now the field is dead config. Nothing in triggarr/ reads `shutdown_drain_timeout`. triggarr/search/scheduler.py:58-81 still takes `_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` only from the TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT env var, once at import time, as a module constant. The planning files for phase 75 (75-01..75-04-PLAN.md, 75-PATTERNS.md under .planning/phases/75-drain-timeout-config-parity-deferred-record-correction/) cover the wiring, the env-override order and the 3600.0 form clamp in later plans. This commit is the test-first field slice of 75-01, so it is not flagged.

The comment at config.py:136-138 describes behavior that is not built yet: config as the default, env override applied at shutdown, and a form clamp at 3600.0. A grep of triggarr/ finds no 3600.0 drain clamp in routes.py, and the scheduler reads the env var at import time, not at shutdown. If phase 75 stops after 75-01, the comment will misstate how the code behaves. Plans 75-02 and 75-03 must land before release.

Design risk when the field is wired up: the drain timeout will have two sources of truth with different validation. The Pydantic field uses ge=1.0 and allow_inf_nan=False. The existing env reader `_read_shutdown_drain_timeout` uses `max(float(raw), 1.0)`. That still lets +inf through, and NaN as well, because max(nan, 1.0) returns nan in CPython. So the env path can still unbound the drain, which the config-field comment says must not happen. This code predates the diff, but the plan text mentions a 'non-finite drain guard' and isfinite. A follow-up should check that the env reader gets the same finite-only guard, ideally by validating both sources through one helper.

The scheduler reads the env var into a module constant at import time, while GeneralConfig is loaded at runtime. When the field is wired in, the drain timeout must be resolved at shutdown from live config plus env, not frozen at import. Otherwise an edit made in the UI would not take effect until restart. Pending: confirm that 75-02/75-03 resolve it at shutdown, as the comment says.
No new imports, dependencies, cycles, cross-module reach-ins or duplication are introduced. models/config.py still imports only pydantic and pydantic_settings.

agent_notes: Change class: adds one new optional field that has a default and tightened validation (ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False). This is a safe change on the validation axis. Existing config.toml files have no such key, so they load unchanged with the 60.0 default. No existing input that used to be accepted is now rejected.

Public API: GeneralConfig gains a field and none are removed or renamed. The 9 importers of models/config.py are unaffected. The config export at routes.py:227 (settings.general.model_dump()) will now include shutdown_drain_timeout, which adds output but breaks nothing.

Validation scope: a TOML config with shutdown_drain_timeout < 1.0, inf or nan now fails to load at startup. No deployment could have such a value, because the field did not exist before. The env var path (scheduler.py:70) is separate and keeps its own clamp to at least 1.0.

Gap in the env path (it predates this diff and is out of scope): the scheduler's _read_shutdown_drain_timeout may accept TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT=inf, depending on how it parses. The new allow_inf_nan guard covers only the TOML path. Worth checking when the env override is combined with the config value.
Schema/DB/perf: no database or migration impact, and no performance impact. This is a single float on a config model that is validated when the config loads.

Blast radius: minimal right now, because nothing consumes the field. The main follow-up risk is save_settings (routes.py:539-551) dropping the field on every UI save until the form wiring lands (impact-1).
Verdict: shippable as an intermediate commit. Before the phase is called complete, wire the field into save_settings and into the scheduler's drain read.

findings.problem: This diff adds `GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout` (models/config.py:139), but `save_settings` (routes.py:539-551) builds the whole `general` dict from a fixed list of keys and does not include the new field. The value is lost silently the moment the field is wired in. As of this commit, the config field is checked when the config loads but has no effect on behavior.
